feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. The candidate is the iteration 1 design, reproduced exactly in iteration 6 (score 75.97, s-bend progress 0.29, oval 0.16, max_error about 0.061 to 0.065 on every track). It keeps kp 2.0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.4, ki 0, last_direction, weights -2..2, sensors at x -0.02..0.02 and y 0.04, and sensor_size 0.012. Every alternative raced since then scored lower: base_speed 1.2 with kd 0.1 (iteration 2, 50.60), kp 2.5 with kd 0.1 (iteration 3, 49.59), wider sensor spacing (iteration 4, 57.85), sensor_size 0.016 (iteration 5, 59.03), kd 0.15 (iteration 7, 57.61), and base_speed 1.5 (iteration 8, 68.89). Approving it races the best known design, which is the safest score for this iteration. Note that max_error has stayed at 0.061 to 0.065 under every controller and geometry tried, so the off-track failure is not fixed by the levers so far. Read the next race as follows. If it reproduces about 76, the baseline is confirmed and the next iteration should test a single lever against it. If progress falls clearly below 0.29 on the s-bend, the earlier result was partly seed-dependent and the design should be judged on all tracks together. Keep ki at 0 unless rms_error shows a steady offset.
requested_changes: If the race reproduces about 76 with s-bend progress near 0.29, test kd 0.25 with everything else unchanged. In the evidence, s-bend progress rose with kd: 0.155 at kd 0.1 (iteration 2), 0.155 at kd 0.15 (iteration 7), and 0.29 at kd 0.2 (iterations 1 and 6). kd 0.25 is the next untested point on that trend.
Keep kp at 2.0. Iteration 3 (kp 2.5, kd 0.1) left max_error at 0.062 to 0.065, so raising kp has not reduced the off-track error.

Do not raise base_speed above 1.4 yet. Iteration 8 (base 1.5, kd 0.2) raised oval progress from 0.16 to 0.22 but cut s-bend progress from 0.29 to 0.167, so speed trades one track against another. Compare any speed change against the s-bend and oval together.
